findings.title: WordPress 7.0.2 Release (Security Release)
findings.summary_md: The WordPress security team shipped fixes for a facilitated SQL injection reported by TF1T, dtro, and haongo, and for a REST API batch-route confusion plus SQL injection leading to Remote Code Execution reported by Adam Kues at Assetnote / Searchlight Cyber. Backports fixed both issues in 6.9.5 and the SQL injection alone in 6.8.6; the 7.1 beta also received the fixes in beta2. Versions prior to WordPress 6.8 are not affected.

findings.title: CVE-2026-60137: WordPress WP_Query author__not_in SQL Injection
findings.summary_md: NVD published the record for insufficient sanitization of the author__not_in parameter in WP_Query, allowing SQL injection when a plugin or theme passes untrusted input to it. Affected versions are 6.8.x before 6.8.6, 6.9.x before 6.9.5, and 7.0.x before 7.0.2. Base score is 5.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N).

findings.title: CVE-2026-63030: WordPress REST API batch endpoint route confusion to RCE
findings.summary_md: NVD published the record for a REST API batch endpoint route confusion issue that, combined with the author__not_in SQL injection (CVE-2026-60137), can achieve Remote Code Execution. Affected versions are 6.9.x before 6.9.5 and 7.0.x before 7.0.2. Base score is 9.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

findings.title: CISA KEV catalog entries for CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030
findings.summary_md: CISA added both WordPress vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-07-21, four days after the fixes shipped. The batch-route RCE chain carried a remediation due date of 2026-07-24 and the SQL injection 2026-08-04, reflecting confirmed exploitation rather than theoretical risk.

findings.title: TIKTouk: Tracing a WordPress Credential Collection Toolkit (LevelBlue SpiderLabs)
findings.summary_md: SpiderLabs researcher Maor Gabay published the original analysis of TIKTouk a day before the story's first coverage, including real-world incident telemetry: a victim host pulled payloads from and reported to controller 31.56[.]58.59, with additional panels at 193.32.162[.]134 and 195.178.110[.]209. A leaked TIKTouk panel examined by analyst Leon Cottrell held roughly 50k server-side credentials across about 37k domains, including hundreds of actor-validated live AWS keys with SES/EC2/Bedrock abuse potential. The post also lists SHA-256 hashes for wp2s_poll.py, wp2s_crack.py, and jscrawl-amd64, and a related Golang botnet binary with remote command execution.
